title: Rahul Gandhi calls plan to use voter ID, not Aadhaar, for welfare payments a 'conspiracy'
dek: Union minister Lalan Singh said voter ID numbers and biometrics would replace Aadhaar as the basis for payments to beneficiaries; no order has been issued and no scheme named.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday accused the Centre of plotting to tie welfare benefits to voter ID cards, after a Union minister said Aadhaar would no longer be the basis for payments to beneficiaries and that voter ID (EPIC) numbers and biometrics would be used instead.

Mr Gandhi linked the plan to the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which the opposition says has struck genuine voters off the lists. "Today, Panchayati Raj schemes. Tomorrow, rations? Pensions? MGNREGA? Housing? Scholarships? Reservations?" he wrote on X. The government has not issued any order making the change, and no scheme has been named.

## What the minister said

Rajiv Ranjan Singh, known as Lalan Singh, the Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, made the remarks at the National Workshop on the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27, organised by the Panchayati Raj ministry in New Delhi, according to reports. Speaking in Hindi, he said "the Aadhaar card will no longer be the basis" for payments to beneficiaries, and that "biometrics and their voter ID (EPIC) number will be used as the basis", reports said. He also said an Aadhaar card could be made "for anyone within five minutes".

He did not say which schemes would use the voter ID number or when the change would take effect, and no notification, circular or Cabinet decision has been reported. The Panchayati Raj ministry had not issued a clarification by Friday night.

## Which payments use Aadhaar now

No Panchayati Raj ministry scheme pays money directly into individual bank accounts, one report noted. But Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts are used for direct benefit transfers under several of the largest central schemes, including PM-Kisan payments to farmers, rural housing under PMAY-G, the National Social Assistance Programme's old-age, widow and disability pensions, and wages under the rural job guarantee scheme. Aadhaar is also required under a National Livestock Mission programme run by the minister's other department, the report said.

Any move to replace Aadhaar with the voter ID number would matter for people who are not on the electoral rolls, including those under 18 and people whose names are removed in a revision.

## The opposition's case

Mr Gandhi called the move a "conspiracy". "Under the guise of SIR, millions of names are being struck off voter lists," he wrote, adding: "A poor person's pension cannot be enslaved to their voter card." He called it "not just vote theft, but rights theft", and claimed that BJP governments in Bihar and West Bengal had already begun implementing such a step; he did not give details, and the claim could not be verified.

He also attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, calling him a "Modi government employee". The Election Commission has rejected the opposition's allegations of "vote theft" in the past.

## The debate dare

The exchange came as Mr Gandhi and Home Minister Amit Shah traded challenges over the SIR. At a rally in Karnal, Haryana, on Thursday, Mr Shah offered a special session of Parliament on the SIR if the Congress wrote to the Prime Minister, and said Mr Gandhi would "just run away" from the answers, according to reports.

On Friday Mr Gandhi posted a video of Mr Shah's remarks alongside a December 2025 statement in which Mr Shah told Parliament that the SIR could not be debated there because the Election Commission is an independent body. "Amit Shah ji, don't confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me. Any platform, any time," Mr Gandhi wrote, in a translation of his Hindi post published in reports.

## What happens next

Whether the minister's remarks turn into a formal order, and for which schemes, is the next thing to watch: any change to how benefits are paid would need notifications from the ministries that run them. The government has not responded to Mr Gandhi's charge that the plan is linked to the SIR, and the debate over a special session of Parliament remains unresolved.
